text: Why did adding larger buffers to network equipment make interactive performance worse?
choices: Larger buffers are slower to access
TCP uses loss as its congestion signal; a large buffer hides congestion by queueing instead of dropping, so the window keeps growing and every packet is delayed by the full queue depth
explanation: The observable result is that a large upload makes an unrelated video call unusable on a connection with plenty of capacity. AQM — CoDel, FQ-CoDel, PIE, CAKE — drops based on how long a packet has been queued rather than on queue occupancy.
